title: Ingest Shield: schema enforcer and sampled-trace handoff for high-volume structured logs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: several services are emitting mixed-format logs (json/plaintext) and inconsistent correlation fields which leads to broken joinability in Loki dashboards and increased cardinality. At peak ingestion, upstream services also trigger bursts that exceed downstream writer throughput, causing packet drops and opaque errors for customers.

Goal: implement an "Ingest Shield" middleware in the telemetry ingest layer that: (1) validates and normalizes structured logs to a stable canonical schema, (2) enforces presence and canonicalization of correlation identifiers (trace_id/span_id/request_id) when available, and (3) performs sampled-trace handoff so that sampled tracing context is attached to a small percentage of high-throughput events without amplifying cardinality or storage. The component must support dynamic schema adapters to avoid hard deploys for application-side schema tweaks.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Ingest pipeline rejects/rewrites malformed JSON with a policy that returns backpressure metrics rather than silent drops.
2) All structured events forwarded to Loki include the canonical 'r_trace' field when a trace header is present, normalized to 32-char hex.
3) Sampled-trace handoff attaches 'r_trace_sampling' tag on <= 2% of high-volume log streams controlled by feature flags.
4) No >5% increase in Loki cardinality for 95th percentile tenants after rollout.
5) Observability dashboards surface: rejected-count, normalized-count, sampling-rate per service, and backpressure events.
6) End-to-end test harness that simulates burst traffic and validates no data loss beyond intended rejects.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (Spike, 1 week): prototype a small middleware that runs as a K8s sidecar for one noisy service (payments-ingest). Validate schema normalization and trace canonicalization.
Phase 2 (Core implementation, 3 sprints): add schema adapter registry, validation rules, and decoupled sampling controller (rate-limit by tenant and tag). Implement graceful NACK/backpressure mechanism to upstream (HTTP 429 with retry-after where supported).
Phase 3 (Integration, 1 sprint): wire into Kafka consumer path that feeds Loki forwarder; add metrics and tracing hooks.
Phase 4 (Canary & rollout, 2 weeks): enable for a subset of tenants then expand.

Key technical decisions & trade-offs:
- Use a lightweight JSON schema subset for validation to avoid computational overhead; reject or rewrite (coerce types) based on configurable policy.
- Store canonical correlation mapping as single string 'r_trace' to avoid multi-field joins; preserve original headers in a raw_payload blob for debugging.
- Sampling controller will be token-bucket per-tenant to limit cross-tenant amplification.
- Backpressure will be signaled via HTTP 429 or Kafka throttling; we prefer explicit NACK to avoid silent loss.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy sidecar prototype to 'payments-ingest' canary namespace with sampling disabled, observe normalized_count metric for 48h.
2) Enable sampling at 0.1% for the same namespace and verify dashboards.
3) Gradually increase to 2% for tenants with heavy traffic while monitoring Loki cardinality and cost signals.
4) If cardinality > threshold, rollback sampling and tighten schema rules.
5) Full cluster rollout behind a feature flag; apply tenant whitelists for initial 30 days.
